Muralee Krishna, J.

This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India by the petitioners seeking the following reliefs:
"(i) declare that the petitioners are entitled to compensation for the property having an extent of 16.50 cents in Sy. Nos.937 and 936/5 of Nadama Village in Kanayannur Taluk and direct respondents 4 and 6 to effect payment of compensation to the petitioners immediately before taking physical possession of the property in question;
(ii) issue a writ of mandamus or order or direction commanding 4th respondent to consider and pass orders on Exhibit P18 claim statement and effect payment of compensation to the petitioners for the land acquired (16.50 cents in Sy. Nos. 937 and 936/5 of Nadama Village in Kanayannur Taluk) forthwith with all consequential benefits and interest"
2.

The grievance of the petitioners is that the property having an extent of 16.50 cents in survey Nos.
936/5 and 937 of Nadama Village, which belong to the 1 st petitioner, were acquired for the construction of Kochi Metro by the 6th respondent Kochi Metro Rail Corporation Ltd, without paying compensation to the Devaswom.
According to the petitioners, Sree Poornathrayeesha 2025:KER:39929 Temple, Tripunithura, is administered and managed by the 1 st petitioner, the Cochin Devaswom Board.

An extent of 7.5 cents in survey No.936 and the buildings therein were acquired by the Government as per proceedings No.L1-1075/16 dated 19.04.1941, by which survey No.936 was subdivided into survey Nos. 936/4 and 936/5.

Since building in survey Nos. 936 and 937 were lying contiguously; the property comprised in survey No. 937, having an extent of 9 cents,
was also acquired by the Government as per proceedings dated 20 May 1944.

The properties were acquired for the functioning of three offices viz.,
(i) Poonithura Devaswom office, (ii) Nadama Devaswom office, and (iii) Vadayampadi patta pravurthy office.
The aforementioned offices were functioning in the buildings situated on the property till 1971.
Thereafter, the buildings were leased out to a tenant.
After the eviction of the tenant as directed in court proceedings, the buildings were demolished in the year 2007.

While the 1st petitioner was in possession and enjoyment of the properties, the additional 7th respondent,
Mallika Thampuran, filed W.P.(C)No.32445 of 2006 inter alia, praying for a direction to 2025:KER:39929 correct the revenue records in respect of the property.
The 1 st petitioner, Cochin Devaswom Board, was arrayed as the 1 st respondent in that writ petition.

3 contended that the property belonged to the Devaswom and not to the petitioner in that writ petition.
By Ext.P6 judgment dated 20.06.2007, this Court dismissed the writ petition and directed the petitioner therein to approach the competent civil court for declaration of title.
Against that judgment, the additional 7 th respondent filed W.A. No.1882 of 2007, and the same was also dismissed vide Ext.P7 judgment dated 31.07.2007.

Thereafter, the additional 7 th respondent,
Mallika Thampuran, filed O.S No.951 of 2008 before the Subordinate Judge's Court, Ernakulam.
The State of Kerala, the Land Revenue Commissioner and the Re-survey Superintendent were also parties to that original suit.
By Ext.P8 judgment dated 26.03.2010, the suit was dismissed by the learned Subordinate Judge.

The judgment was challenged before this Court by filing R.F.A. No.561 of 2010, and this Court passed Ext.P9 order dated 06.04.2015 in I.A. No.722 of 2015 filed in the R.F.A. by the appellant therein, turning down the request for an 2025:KER:39929 interim order.
When petitioners came to know about the proposal for the acquisition of the property for Kochi Metro, they submitted Ext.P18 claim statement before the 4 th respondent, Special Tahsildar.
However, no orders have been passed in Ext.P18.
Hence, the petitioners approached this Court.

3. On 05.09.2019 when this writ petition came up for consideration, this Court noted the pendency of R.F.A. No.561 of 2010 filed against the judgment and decree in O.S No.951 of 2008, wherein the issue whether the properties involved in this writ petition is puramboku land or not was under consideration and adjourned the matter awaiting the outcome of the R.F.A.
4.
On 14.11.2019, as per the order in I.A. No.1 of 2019, additional respondents 7 and 8 were impleaded in the writ petition.

5. Additional respondents 7 and 8 filed a counter affidavit dated 01.01.2020 denying the averments in the writ petition and contending that the property belonged to those respondents and they are entitled to the compensation for the acquired land.
6. The 6th respondent filed a counter affidavit dated 2025:KER:39929 12.06.2020, producing therewith Ext.R6(a) copy of the extract of the basic tax register of the property in question.
The 6 th respondent contended that the property claimed by the petitioners absolutely belongs to the Government, and the petitioners and the additional 7th respondent have no right over the property.

For road widening of Petta S.N. Junction Section of NH 85 (Kochi-Madurai- Dhanushkodi National Highway), notifications were published by the 4th respondent under Section 11 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013 ('LARR Act' for short) on 07.03.2018 for the acquisition of 98.26 Ares of Land.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The proposed acquisition was as preparatory work for the Kochi Metro line extension from Petta to Tripunithura by widening the road.
The land involved in the writ petition is a Government (Purambokku) land as per the village records and survey records.

The 6th respondent filed an additional counter affidavit dated 29.06.2020, producing therewith Ext.R6(b) document, however, stating that the total extent of land in survey Nos. 937 and 936/5 proposed to be acquired after resurvey is 6.32 Ares, and the entire 2025:KER:39929 land is urgently required for completing the project and Ext.R6(b) request dated 25.06.2020 was given to the District Collector for transferring the land.

It is further stated in the counter affidavit that if in R.F.A. No.561 of 2010, this Court finds the ownership over the land as not of the Government, the eligible compensation can be paid to the owner.

sentences.text: To the counter affidavits, the petitioners filed a reply affidavit dated 17.09.2020, producing therewith Ext.P21 true copy of the judgment dated 26.08.2020 in R.F.A. No. 561 of 2010, whereby the R.F.A. was dismissed by this Court, upholding the judgment in the suit.
8. The 3rd respondent filed a counter affidavit dated 23.06.2022, producing therewith Exts.R3(a) to R3(e) documents.

It is contended by the 3rd respondent that though the land in dispute was acquired by the State in the years 1941 and 1944 respectively, and Vadayampadi Patta Pravurthi office, Poonithura Devaswom Office and Nadama Devaswom Office started functioning therein, the land was not transferred or conveyed to anybody, much less the petitioners.

It is further contended by the 2025:KER:39929 3rd respondent that the disputed land situated in Block No.224/15 (old survey No.936/5) having an extent of 3.10 Ares and 3.22 Ares in resurvey Block No.224 /16 (old survey No.937) of Nadama village are termed as sarkar purambokku in the revenue records.
The land in resurvey No.224/16 is then subdivided and assigned with resurvey No.224/37, which was given for Kochi Metro Rail Project alignment by the office of Special Tahsildar (LA) No.1.
The remaining land, lying vacant was unauthorisedly occupied by Hotel Saravanabhavan to provide parking place for their customers.

This area was later evicted in accordance with law, and now the land is under the exclusive possession of the Government and is being used for storing the construction material of the Metro Rail project with permission.

9. Heard Sri K.P Sudheer, the learned Standing Counsel for Cochin Devaswom Board,
Sri.Hanilkumar M.H, the learned Special Government Pleader, Sri.P.A Augustine (Areekattel), the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 6 th respondent Kochi Metro Rail Corporation and Sri.Vivek Varghese P.J, the learned counsel for the additional respondents 7 and 8.
2025:KER:39929 10.

The learned Standing Counsel for the petitioners would submit that the property in question was acquired by the State in the years 1941 and 1944, respectively, for the purpose of functioning of Devaswom Offices.

From Ext.P3 Thanathu Register, Ext.P11 certificate dated 20.08.2009 issued by the Tahsildar of Kanayannur Taluk, Ext.P12 extract of building tax assessment register and also from Ext.P21 judgment of this Court in R.F.A. No.561 of 2010, it is evident that the property in question has been in the possession of the 1st petitioner Cochin Devaswom Board by putting up a building therein.

As per Section 62 of the Travancore Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act,1950,
('the Act' in short)

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: , the property has been vested in the Cochin Devaswom Board.
It was without giving notice to the Board, the property was handed over by the Government to the 6 th respondent,
Kochi Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.
After the filing of the writ petition, the project of Kochi Metro in a portion of the disputed property was completed.
The property ought to have been acquired following the procedure for acquisition, and the compensation ought to have been paid to the 1st petitioner Board.

In Ext.P8 judgment dated 2025:KER:39929 26.03.2010 passed by the Sub Court,
Ernakulam in O.S. No.951 of 2008, the claim of the additional 7 th and 8th respondents was found against them and the suit was dismissed.
This finding was confirmed in the first appeal filed by them before this Court, and as per Ext.P21 judgment, wherein it was found that the property has been in the possession of the 1 st petitioner.

In short, the learned Standing Counsel vehemently argued that the compensation for the acquired portion of the disputed property has to be paid to the Cochin Devaswom Board vs State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154338904/
5

sentences.text: 1st petitioner by the 6th respondent

The learned Government Pleader argued that it is true that the portions of the properties in question were acquired in the years 1941 and 1944 respectively, by the Government, for the functioning of the Devaswom Offices.
However, the ownership of the property was not transferred to the Devaswom or to the 1st petitioner.
The offices of the Devaswom had been functioning on the property as permitted by the Government.
There will be no automatic vesting of the ownership of the property to the 1 st petitioner by virtue of Section 62 of the Act, since the occupation of the property was on a permissive basis.

Ext.R6(a) extract of the 2025:KER:39929 basic tax register of the property situated in survey Nos.936/5 and 937 of Nadama Village would show that the property is still in the ownership of the Government.
Even after resurvey, the property is shown as purambokku, and the petitioners have not challenged the said entry by invoking the provisions under Section 13 of the Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act.
In Ext.P8 judgment also the property is found as a purambokku land and hence the petitioners cannot claim title over the same.

12. The learned counsel for the 6 th respondent also supported the arguments of the learned Government Pleader and submitted that there are no acquisition proceedings in respect of Government lands and hence the compensation was not deposited in the competent Court, taking it as a matter of dispute between the parties on title.
The learned counsel for additional respondents 7 and 8 maintained their stand in Exts.P8 suit and P21 appeal that they are the owners of the property.
13. We have carefully gone through the materials on record and the rival submissions made at the Bar.

The petitioners are claiming title and possession over an extent of 16.50 cents of land 2025:KER:39929 in survey Nos.937 and 936/5 of Nadama Village in Kanayannur Taluk, a portion of which is utilised for the Cochin Metro Rail Project.
According to the petitioners, the property ought to have been acquired following the procedure for land acquisition, and the compensation ought to have been paid to the 1 st petitioner.

But according to the respondents 1 to 6, the property is a Government land shown as purambokku in the revenue records, and hence there is no necessity to acquire the property, and the petitioners cannot raise any claim on the same.

The property in dispute was acquired by the erstwhile Cochin Sarkar in the years 1941 and 1944 respectively, for the purpose of running the Devaswom offices such as Poonithura Devaswom Office, Nadama Devaswom Office, and Vadayampadi Patta Pravurthy Office.
Till the year 2007, those office buildings existed therein, and it was demolished in that year.

From Ext.P3 Thanathu register, Ext.P5 survey settlement register, Ext.P11 certificate issued by the Tahsildar of Kanayannur Taluk and Ext.P12 extract of building tax register, it could be gathered that the Devaswom offices had been functioning on the property in question, which is admitted by the respondents 2025:KER:39929 also.
At the same time, Ext.R6(a) extract of the basic tax register would show that the property still stands in the name of the State Government as a purambokku land.

14. Ext.P8 judgment produced by the petitioners would show that additional respondents 7 and 8 had previously filed a suit as O.S. No. 951 of 2008 before the Sub Court, Ernakulam, for partition and consequential reliefs, claiming title and possession over the property in dispute.
The petitioners and respondents herein were all made parties in the said suit.

As per Ext.P8 judgment dated Cochin Devaswom Board vs State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154338904/
6 26.03.2010, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the additional respondents 7 and 8 herein could not prove their co-ownership right or possession over the property, and there is insufficient material to come to a conclusion that the property in survey No. 937 is not a purambokku land.

entities.text: Cochin Devaswom Board vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Ext.P21 judgment dated 26.08.2020 in R.F.A. No.561 of 2020 filed by additional respondents 7 and 8, this Court found that the petitioners herein had made out a strong case of possession of the property.
However, while going through Exts.P8 and P21 judgments, we notice that a clear finding regarding title over the 2025:KER:39929 property is not arrived at in those cases.
The only finding is the inability of additional respondents 7 and 8 to prove their title and co-ownership as claimed in the suit.
The interse dispute between the petitioners herein and respondents 1 to 5 regarding ownership of the property is not decided in Exts.P8 and P21 judgments.

15. In such circumstances, we are of the view that the rival contentions regarding title raised by the parties, that is, whether the property is that of the 1st petitioner, Cochin Devaswom Board or that of the 1st respondent, State have to be decided in a properly instituted civil suit.

At this juncture the learned counsel for the petitioners invited our attention to the judgment of this Court in Cochin Devaswom Board v. Union of India [2023 (6) KHC 328] and submitted that in that case this Court held that merely based on the entry in the resurvey and revenue records that the property in that matter as purambokku would not have the effect of ousting title of the Devaswom.

entities.text: Cochin Devaswom Board v. Union of India [2023 (6) KHC 328]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But while going through the facts of that case, we notice that the property in dispute therein was the Devaswom property and not a property acquired by the Government for functioning of the Devaswom 2025:KER:39929 Offices, as that in the instant case.
In such circumstances, the judgment in that case is not applicable to the case in hand.

In the result, the writ petition is disposed of, leaving open all the legal and factual contentions raised by the parties in this writ petition to be decided in a properly instituted civil suit before the competent Civil Court.

The petitioners are granted liberty to institute such a civil suit before the competent Civil Court within two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, and in that event in computing the period of limitation, they are entitled for exclusion of time of the period during which they bona fide prosecuted the writ petition before this Court.
